chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Bakr ibn Salih, who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: For the wind that sticks (gastric trouble), and the heaviness, and the coldness in the joints, take a handful of fenugreek and a handful of dry figs, submerge them in water, and cook them in a clean pot. Then strain it, then cool it, then drink from it one day and skip the next, until you have drunk from it for the completion of your days, in the measure of a full cup.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended herbal remedy for stomach wind and joint coldness in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) prescribes a specific herbal decoction of fenugreek and dry figs for treating joint ailments (Rih al-Shabika) and gastrointestinal issues, reflecting the Shia tradition of integrating practical medicine with spiritual guidance. The regimen of consuming the strained liquid every other day highlights the Prophetic emphasis on moderation and the therapeutic value of natural ingredients found in the Sunnah.

en.hubeali: H 14669 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from bakr Bin Saleh who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hassan the Firstasws saying: ‘The one with wind (gastric trouble), and Al-Haam, and the coldness in the joints should take a handful of fenugreek (plant) and a handful of dry fig, soak these two in the water, and cook these two in a clean pot, then drain it, then cool it, then drink from it every other day until the completeness of your days the measurement of a cup’.
